title: Jack and Jill: Why Is Winter Ice So Slippery?

lines.text: Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water!
lines.caps: Jack and Jill went *UP | the hill to fetch a pail of *WATER!

lines.text: Jack fell down and broke his crown, slipping on the slick winter ice!
lines.caps: Jack fell *DOWN | and broke his crown, *SLIPPING | on the slick winter *ICE!

lines.text: Why is smooth ice so much more slippery than hard wooden floors?
lines.caps: Why is smooth *ICE | so much more slippery than hard *WOODEN | *FLOORS?

lines.text: At the very surface of ice, water molecules cannot hold onto each other tightly!
lines.caps: At the very *SURFACE | of ice, water molecules cannot *HOLD | onto each other *TIGHTLY!

lines.text: They form an ultra-thin layer of loose, slushy liquid water molecules!
lines.caps: They form an ultra-thin *LAYER | of loose, slushy liquid *WATER | *MOLECULES!

lines.text: When your warm boot steps down, that microscopic water layer acts like ball bearings!
lines.caps: When your warm boot steps *DOWN, | that microscopic water layer *ACTS | like ball *BEARINGS!

lines.text: There's almost zero friction, which lets your feet glide—or tumble down the hill!
lines.caps: There's almost zero *FRICTION, | which lets your feet *GLIDE— | or tumble down the *HILL!

lines.text: Now you know the slippery physics behind Jack and Jill!
lines.caps: Now you *KNOW | the slippery *PHYSICS | behind Jack and *JILL!

lines.text: Tread carefully and subscribe to BabyBeats Rhymo for daily facts!
lines.caps: *TREAD carefully and | *SUBSCRIBE to | *BABYBEATS Rhymo | for daily *FACTS!
